Rashi on Shabbat 53b:10:1.hebrew: שהיה תחום שלה מובלעת בתוך תחום שלו - דחוץ לתחום דקתני, חוץ לתחום שלה; שהבהמה המסורה לרועה המיוחד הרי היא כרגלי הרועה, וזה הקורא לה — בעליה, ויכול לילך, כגון שהוא שבת קרוב לאותו מקום. ואפילו הכי, לא יביאנה ממש בידיו, הואיל והיא יצאה חוץ לתחומה אין לה אלא ד' אמות. ומיהו, קורא לה והיא באה, דלא הוזהר הוא על תחום בהמתו, ובלבד שלא יביאנה ממש בידיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:10:1.english: Where its limit was subsumed within his limit - For that which [the baraita] teaches, "beyond the limit," [means] beyond its limit; for an animal entrusted to a dedicated shepherd is like the feet of the shepherd, and this one who calls to it is its owner, and he is able to go [there] — for instance, where he spent Shabbat close to that place. And even so, he may not literally bring it with his hands, since it went beyond its limit, [and therefore] it has only four cubits. However, he may call to it and it will come, for he is not commanded regarding the limit of his animal, provided that he does not literally bring it with his hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna’im - For there is [an authority] who did not decree [against] other remedies on account of crushing herbs.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:2.hebrew: שאכלה כרשינין - הרבה, ועל ידי אכילה מרובה אחזה חולי שקורין מינייזונ"א, וצריכה להשתלשל ולהוציא רעי, ומריצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:2.english: That ate vetch - [It ate] a great deal, and through excessive eating an illness seized it that they call meneisons [diarrhea], and it needs to loosen its bowels and expel dung, and [so] he runs it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:3.hebrew: כדי שתתרפה - גרסינן הכא לשון ריפוי: שיהיו מיעיה רפויים בשילשול, ומוציאה רעי:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:3.english: In order that it be loosened - Our reading here is an expression of loosening: that its bowels will be loosened through diarrhea, and it will discharge excrement.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:11:4.english: One may not run it - [It is] a decree regarding all healing, lest [one come to] grind herbs.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:13:1.english: [That is] fastened tightly - For there is no concern lest it fall and he come to bring it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:14:1.hebrew: תנאי שקלת מעלמא - איבדת כולם, שאין אתה מוצא תנאים שנחלקו בכך, דתוקי הנך תרתי מתניית' חדא כמר וחדא כמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:14:1.english: Have you removed the tanna’im from the world? - Did you eliminate all of them, that you cannot find tanna’im who disagree about this, so that you [could] establish these two teachings — one according to [this] Master and one according to [that] Master?

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:14:2.hebrew: תנאי היא - במתניתין: ר"מ שרי, ר' יוסי אסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:14:2.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna’im - In our Mishnah: Rabbi Meir permits [it], [and] Rabbi Yosei prohibits [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:15:1.hebrew: ליבש - מיהדק שפיר. ולענין משוי נמי לא הוי משוי, דצורך גופה היא, דחלבה מכחישה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:15:1.english: To dry - It is fastened well. And regarding the matter of a burden as well, it is not a burden, for it is for the need of its [own] body, as its milk emaciates it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:15:2.hebrew: ליחלב - הוי משוי, שטוענת את החלב בכיס:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:15:2.english: To be milked - It is a burden, as she carries the milk in the pouch.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:16:1.hebrew: גסין - גדולין, ונגררין על הקוצין, ומסרטין דדיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:16:1.english: Large - Large, and [they] drag along the thorns, and [the thorns] scratch their udders.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:19:1.english: That [the order of creation] was altered for him, etc. - And he did not merit that the gates of earnings be opened for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:19:3.english: That miracles are performed - From Heaven for many rescues of human lives.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:19:4.hebrew: ולא איברו מזוני - ואין נס זה רגיל שיבראו מזונות לצדיקים בביתם, שימצאו חיטין גדילין באוצרותיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:19:4.english: And food was not created - And this miracle is not common, that food should be created for the righteous in their homes, [such] that they find wheat growing in their storehouses.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:1:1.english: Similar to an amulet - [Which is worn] on account of illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:20:2.hebrew: זו דרכה בכך - לכסות כל אשה עצמה, וכ"ש זו שהיתה צריכה לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:20:2.english: That is typical conduct for her - For every woman to cover herself, and all the more so this [woman], who needed to do so.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:21:1.hebrew: תותרי - קופל"א, שמחברין אותם בקשר שנים שנים, שלא יברחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:21:1.english: Tutari - Cople [in Old French, i.e., coupled], as they join them with a knot two by two, so that they will not run away.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:21:2.english: You have drawn me near - You have drawn me close to yourself on account of the beauty of your deeds.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:22:1.english: It is the way of wolves to seize an animal by its heart.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:22:2.english: Do they not fall upon females - In astonishment:

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:22:4.english: Do they not attack the rear of the flock - [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:22:5.hebrew: כי דוו - מביטין כאן וכאן. לפיכך מתקנאין בהם, כסבורים שרוצים להלחם בהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:22:5.english: Like [those who] look around - [They] look here and there. Therefore, [the wolves] are provoked against them, thinking that [the rams] want to fight them.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:23:1.hebrew: אליה - זנב שלהן — קושרים כלפי גבן, שלא יכסה ערותן:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:23:1.english: The fat tail - Their tail — they tie [it] toward their back, so that it will not cover their genitalia.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:2:1.hebrew: והא אנן תנן - גבי אדם, לקמן בפ' במה אשה (שבת דף ס.):
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:2:1.english: And didn’t we learn - [This was taught] regarding a person, below in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 60a).

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:2:2.english: By inference, [if it is] effective, it is well - What is the difference between an animal and a person?

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:3:1.english: His mazal - His angel, who advocates on his behalf.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:4:1.english: If so - That an animal may also go out with an amulet that has proven effective for an animal.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:4:2.english: What is [the meaning of] “This is a stricture” - A person, too, does not go out except with an amulet that is proven effective for a person.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:4:3.hebrew: אסנדל קאי - ו״זה חומר״ דקתני — קאי על ״ולא בהמה בסנדל שברגליה״:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:4:3.english: It is referring to a shoe - And that which [the baraita] teaches, "this is a stricture" — [it refers to]: "Nor an animal with a shoe on its feet."

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:5:2.english: And scrape - [The] scabs of a wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:5:3.hebrew: ומשום צער - [ואפילו] הכי, לבהמה לא, וקשיא בין לרב בין לשמואל, דשרי במרדעת:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:5:3.english: And on account of pain - [And even] so, for an animal [it is] not [permitted]; and [this is] difficult both according to Rav and according to Shmuel, who permit [an animal going out] with a packsaddle.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:5:4.hebrew: לא דגמר מכה - שנתרפאה המכה, וסיכה ופירכוס משום תענוג. ולרב ודאי קשיא, וההיא מתניתא קמייתא דאוכף נמי קשיא ליה — דנהי נמי דלצינה ליכא צער, תענוג מיהא הוא! אלא רב תנא הוא ופליג:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:5:4.english: No, where the wound has ended - That the wound has healed, and anointing and scraping [are done] for pleasure. And according to Rav, [this baraita] is certainly difficult, and that first baraita regarding a saddle is also difficult for him — for granted that there is no discomfort from cold, it is at least [done for] pleasure! Rather, Rav is a Tanna and differs.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:6:1.english: [An animal] that was seized by blood - Founder [i.e., equine laminitis or congestion].

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:6:2.english: One may not stand [it], etc. - Evidently, even [in a case of] pain, it is also forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:6:3.hebrew: גזירה משום שחיקת סממנים - במידי דרפואה גזור רבנן, דאי שרית שום רפואה, אתי למישרי שחיקת סממנים; והוא איסורא דאורייתא, דהוי טוחן:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:6:3.english: A decree due to the grinding of herbs - Concerning matters of healing, the Rabbis decreed [a prohibition], for if you permit any healing, one will come to permit the grinding of herbs; and that is a Torah prohibition, as it constitutes [the labor of] grinding.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:8:1.hebrew: אין מיקר לבהמה - אין דרך להקר בהמה. הלכך, כולי עלמא ידעי דלרפואה קמיכוין, ואתי למישרי שחיקת סממנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:8:1.english: There is no cooling for an animal - It is not customary to cool an animal. Therefore, everyone knows that he intends [it] for healing, and they might come to permit the grinding of herbs.

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:9:1.english: And do we issue a decree - In a situation of [financial] loss in a case such as this?

Rashi on Shabbat 53b:9:2.hebrew: חוץ לתחום - קס"ד, חוץ לתחום שלו היתה עומדת בהמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53b:9:2.english: Beyond the [Shabbat] limit - It entered [the Gemara's] mind [to assume that] the animal was standing outside of his [the owner's] Shabbat limit.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:10:1.hebrew: כגון שהיה תחום שלה מובלע כו' - ומ"מ, לא התירו אלא דרך קריאה; אבל לילך מעבר לבהמה ולרודפה לעיר — לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:10:1.english: “For example, where its [Shabbat] limit was subsumed, etc.” - And nevertheless, they only permitted [bringing it back] by way of calling; but to go to the other side of the animal and chase it toward the city — no [that is not permitted].

Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:11:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - רב יהודה ידע שפיר דתנאי היא, אלא דניחא ליה לאוקמי תרי סתמי דברייתא אליבא דחד תנא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:11:1.english: It is a dispute between tanna’im - Rav Yehuda knew full well that it is a dispute between tanna’im, but he preferred to establish two anonymous baraitot in accordance with a single tanna.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:15:1.hebrew: כאן ליבש כאן ליחלב - פי' בקונט': "ליחלב" — שיקבלו בכיס את החלב. וקשה: דהא ודאי משוי הוא, ולכ"ע חייב, דהויא מלאכה הצריכה לגופה! ופי' ה"ר פור"ת: "ליחלב" — לשמור החלב בדדיהן, שלא יזוב לארץ; ושרי ת"ק, דהוי כמו "רחלים כבונות", דחשבי' ליה מלבוש, אף על פי שאינו עשוי לצורך עצמן אלא לשמור הצמר. ור"י פירש: דבין ליבש ובין ליחלב — תרווייהו עבדי להו כדי שלא יסרטו דדיהן, כדאמרינן בסמוך; וליבש, בזמן שאינו חפץ בחלב — שרי, לפי שמהדקו, וליכא למיחש דילמא נפיל ואתי לאתויי; אבל ליחלב, שאינו רוצה שיתייבשו — אינו מיהדק, איכא למימר דילמא נפיל ואתי לאתויי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:15:1.english: “Here to dry, there to be milked” - The Kuntres explained: “To be milked” — that they collect the milk in the pouch. And this is difficult: For that is certainly a burden, and according to everyone one is liable, as it is a labor needed for its own sake! And Rabbeinu Porat explained: “To be milked” means to preserve the milk in their udders so that it does not flow out onto the ground; and the First Tanna permits this, as it is like “shrouded ewes,” which we consider a garment for it, even though it is not made for the sake of the animals themselves, but rather to protect the wool. And the Ri explained that both “to dry” and “to be milked” — both of them are done so that their udders will not be scratched, as we say nearby in the Gemara; and “to dry,” at a time when he has no desire for the milk, is permitted because he fastens it tightly, and there is no concern lest it fall and he come to bring it; but “to be milked,” where he does not want the udders to dry up, he does not fasten it tightly, and there is reason to say lest it fall and he come to bring it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:23:1.hebrew: שקושרין להן כנגד זכרותן כו' - ולשון "לבובין" הוי שלא לקרב, כמו "ובכל תבואתי תשרש" (איוב לד), וכמוהו הרבה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:23:1.english: "That they tie for them opposite their male organ, etc." - And the term "levuvin" means not to bring close, like: "And in all my produce it would root out" (Job 34), and there are many [instances] like it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:23:2.hebrew: ממאי מדקתני סיפא - טפי הוי ליה לאתויי כבולות, דהוי ממש כעין זה; אלא משום דשחוזות הוי ברישא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53b:23:2.english: "From where? From that which the latter clause teaches" - It would have been better to cite [the case of] kevulot, which is literally just like this; rather, [the Gemara cites sheḥuzot] because sheḥuzot appears first [in the Mishnah].
